title: Tencent ORIDTP Designs Dual-Target Obesity and Cancer Immunotherapy Peptides in Nature
whyItMatters: Published in Nature: designs high-potency dual-receptor peptides—GLP-1R/GCGR co-agonists surpassing natural binders without nausea, and zero-shot PD-1/CTLA-4 co-inhibitors cutting mouse tumor volume by 94.2%.
summary: Tencent’s AI for Life Sciences Lab (with Monash University and partner Chinese hospitals) published ORIDTP in Nature, a generative peptide-design framework combining single-target knowledge transfer with dual-target reinforcement learning to engineer single peptides engaging two distinct biological receptors simultaneously. Six ORIDTP-designed GLP-1R/GCGR co-agonists surpassed the strongest natural binders in bioactivity, with lead GA-Dual.R5.S3 producing substantial weight loss and glycemic improvement in obese and db/db mice without nausea or aversion; in a zero-shot test against structurally distinct immune checkpoints PD-1 and CTLA-4, 8 of 15 peptides blocked both targets and lead IC-Dual.P3 reduced tumor volume by 94.2% in humanized-checkpoint mice.
technicalHighlights: Combines single-target knowledge transfer with dual-target reinforcement learning to overcome historically low hit rates for multi-receptor peptide drugs.
Six designed GLP-1R/GCGR co-agonists outperformed natural ligands; lead GA-Dual.R5.S3 drove weight loss and antidiabetic efficacy in obese and db/db mice without nausea.
Zero-shot dual checkpoint campaign against PD-1 and CTLA-4 yielded 8/15 dual blockers and lead IC-Dual.P3 cutting mouse tumor volume by 94.2% vs. controls.
caveats: All efficacy data reported in the Nature paper are preclinical (cell assays and mouse models); human clinical safety, pharmacokinetics, and immunogenicity remain to be tested.
institutions: Tencent AI for Life Sciences Lab

scoreRationale.foundational: Solves the multi-objective dual-receptor peptide engineering bottleneck across both metabolic GPCRs and cancer immune checkpoints.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly targets two of the highest-impact therapeutic classes in modern medicine: GLP-1/glucagon metabolic drugs and checkpoint immunotherapies.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Nature (Nov 25, 2026) with in vitro binding and in vivo mouse validation across two distinct disease areas.
scoreRationale.velocity: Demonstrated zero-shot dual-target immune-checkpoint design succeeding on 8 of just 15 synthesized peptides.
